subject.title: [Feature]: Feature Request: Batch Tool Calls + Context Block Management + Plan Enforcement

question: Should OpenClaw split this umbrella into native batch-tool schemas, AI-managed context block APIs, and strict submitted-plan enforcement, or route any of those tracks to plugin/ClawHub surfaces first?
rationale: The request adds new core tools and config behavior across agent runtime, context/session state, and tool schemas; repository vision says core should stay lean and optional capabilities should usually start in plugins unless a missing core API is proven.

options.title: Split into design tracks
options.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella or split it into maintainer-owned tracks, with context-result lifecycle work linked to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/45503 and runtime-governance overlap linked to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/97371.

options.title: Plugin-first prototypes
options.body: Prototype context/block management or plan governance as plugins where existing hooks suffice, then add only the narrow core seams that prototypes prove are missing.

options.title: Narrow to one core capability
options.body: Pick one highest-value core surface, such as native file/search batching or a canonical context lifecycle API, and defer the remaining tracks until there is separate evidence and ownership.

recommendation.title: Split into design tracks
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella or split it into maintainer-owned tracks, with context-result lifecycle work linked to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/45503 and runtime-governance overlap linked to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/97371.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior live review and nearby plan/runtime history make steipete the strongest available owner for the product-boundary decision.
